node.title: Re: shedding a bash wrapper and updating to Path::Tiny
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
I essentially want to combine what these 2 do
  • chmod: [mod://Path::Tiny] supports a chmod method (e.g. $obj->chmod("0755") or $obj->chmod("a+x")), which it gets from [mod://File::chmod], unfortunately [mod://Path::Class], which you're using in your code, does not, but you can use Perl's [doc://chmod] (just make sure to check for errors). Perl's [doc://chmod] only supports numeric modes, though.
  • cd: [doc://chdir] (make sure to check for errors)
  • pwd: getcwd from [doc://Cwd]

As for your code, it's pretty long and I've only skimmed it for now, but one thing I noticed is that you're using ->stringfiy a lot, into temporary variables. While certainly not wrong, it's kind of cluttering up your code a bit - for debug output, you should be able to [doc://print] the objects directly, and also note that it's not necessary to stringify the objects only to turn them back into objects again later. Using $srd3 as an example:

my $rd3 = dir( ... ); my $srd3 = $rd3->stringify; mkdir $srd3 or warn "couldn't make $srd3: $!\n"; say "srd3 is $srd3"; $b = file( $srd3, $_ );

Can be written instead as:

my $rd3 = dir( ... ); $rd3->mkpath(); say "rd3 is $rd3"; my $f = $rd3->file( $_ );
